discussion_comments.comment_body:
I think it might be but would be happy to talk about it with you.
IMO the worst thing that can happen if there is an error with the hook is that the hook will not be executed and the terminal integration features will not run, but the REPL would function normally. Otherwise, we might pollute the REPL with an error message for every statement run.

I think the question for this is similar in nature to https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/130698 "What should we do when a REPL customization fails?"
